title: Behavioral & Leadership Core
description: Curated behavioral and engineering leadership prompts tagged by competency and level, with CARL coaching hooks.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you took an ambiguous problem from 0 to 1 where nobody had defined the roadmap yet.
follow_ups: What assumptions did you validate first, and which ones turned out to be wrong?
Where did you cut scope to ship something real instead of over-building?
What would you design differently if you started that project over today?
questions.carl_focus: Make your personal framing in Context crisp, highlight concrete trade-offs in Action, and close with a genuine Learning you now reuse.

questions.prompt: Describe a project where you spotted a structural problem outside your immediate scope and decided to own fixing it.
follow_ups: How did you earn buy-in from the team that originally owned that system?
What did you have to deprioritize or negotiate to make time for it?
questions.carl_focus: Explain why you intervened rather than escalating, and show how the fix stuck after you moved on.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to drive cross-team alignment on a technical direction when partner teams had competing priorities.
follow_ups: What was the strongest objection from the skeptical team, and how did you address it?
Did you change part of your proposal based on their feedback?
questions.carl_focus: Show empathy for the other team's constraints before explaining how you built shared alignment.

questions.prompt: Describe a time you convinced engineering leadership or product partners to change course based on data or a prototype.
follow_ups: What made the evidence compelling enough to shift a committed plan?
What was the cost of switching late, and how did you de-risk it?
questions.carl_focus: Pair the prototype/data moment with the concrete business or user outcome in Result.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a strong technical disagreement you had with a peer or senior engineer. How did you work through it?
follow_ups: Looking back, what parts of their argument were actually right?
How did the working relationship feel after the decision landed?
questions.carl_focus: Avoid villainizing the other person — great answers highlight curiosity, principled criteria, and commit-or-disagree maturity.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you pushed back on a product requirement or aggressive deadline because of quality, safety, or reliability concerns.
follow_ups: What alternative path did you propose instead of just saying no?
How did you frame the engineering risk in terms product stakeholders cared about?
questions.carl_focus: Highlight how you offered concrete options and trade-offs rather than a flat veto.

questions.prompt: Walk me through a meaningful technical mistake or launch incident you caused or owned. What happened and what changed afterward?
follow_ups: What was the earliest warning sign you missed in hindsight?
What systemic safeguard did you put in place so a teammate couldn't hit the same trap?
questions.carl_focus: Own the mistake directly without deflecting, then spend half your answer on the systemic Learning.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a feature or architecture you invested significant time into that didn't pan out the way you hoped.
follow_ups: How did you recognize it was time to pivot or sunset it instead of sinking more cost?
How did you communicate that call to stakeholders?
questions.carl_focus: Show intellectual honesty and a clear lesson that changed how you scope future bets.

questions.prompt: Describe a time requirements or priorities shifted mid-project. How did you adapt without losing momentum or quality?
follow_ups: How did you protect the team from thrash while re-scoping?
Which architectural decisions turned out to make the pivot easier or harder?
questions.carl_focus: Explain the decision framework you used under uncertainty, not just the timeline of events.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to make an important technical call with incomplete information and tight time pressure.
follow_ups: How did you distinguish reversible decisions from irreversible ones?
What monitoring or escape hatches did you build in case the bet was wrong?
questions.carl_focus: Emphasize how you bounded risk and what signal told you the call was working.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you raised the bar on code quality, architecture, or developer experience across your team.
follow_ups: How did you get engineers to adopt the standard willingly rather than seeing it as bureaucracy?
How did you measure whether it actually sped people up or reduced bugs?
questions.carl_focus: Ground your standard in a real pain point and show measurable or observable adoption.

questions.prompt: Describe a complex performance, reliability, or debugging investigation where the root cause surprised you.
follow_ups: What dead ends did you rule out along the way, and what instrumentation unlocked the answer?
How did you prevent regressions after fixing it?
questions.carl_focus: Walk cleanly through your hypothesis-testing loop so the interviewer sees structured engineering judgment.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you worked directly with users, customers, or designers to reshape a feature in a way that materially improved the product.
follow_ups: What user insight would you have missed if you had only built from the spec?
How did you balance polish and accessibility with shipping speed?
questions.carl_focus: Connect the user empathy directly to the engineering changes you made and the behavioral shift in Result.

questions.prompt: Describe a time you simplified a complex product or technical workflow instead of adding another knob or feature.
follow_ups: What resistance did you face when proposing to remove or hide complexity?
How did you verify power users weren't hurt by the simplification?
questions.carl_focus: Show taste and judgment: why subtraction beat addition, and what changed for users afterward.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you mentored or unblocked a teammate who was struggling on a high-stakes deliverable.
follow_ups: How did you avoid just taking over the keyboard yourself?
What habits or skills did they carry forward into future projects?
questions.carl_focus: Show coaching craft — how you diagnosed the gap and helped them grow rather than hero-fixing.

questions.prompt: Describe how you've given difficult, constructive feedback to a peer or collaborator. How did you approach it?
follow_ups: How did you prepare so the feedback felt specific and supportive rather than personal?
What changed after that conversation?
questions.carl_focus: Highlight care, specificity, and observable follow-through.

questions.prompt: Tell me about the most technically complex full-stack or multi-system launch you led end to end.
follow_ups: Which integration boundary carried the highest risk, and how did you test it safely?
How did you stage the rollout and decide when it was safe to ramp to 100%?
questions.carl_focus: Keep Context to 30 seconds so you have room for the hardest Action decisions and real launch Result.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you intentionally took on technical debt to hit a critical milestone — and how you managed paying it down later.
follow_ups: How did you isolate the shortcut so it wouldn't spread across the codebase?
Did you actually pay it back, or did it turn out not to matter?
questions.carl_focus: Great pragmatic answers show deliberate boundaries and honest hindsight in Learning.

questions.prompt: Describe a multi-quarter technical strategy or platform migration you conceived and drove across multiple teams.
follow_ups: How did you sequence early wins so teams saw value before the full migration finished?
What parts of the original vision did you have to revise halfway through?
questions.carl_focus: Explain the thesis, sequencing strategy, and org-level adoption metrics clearly.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you evaluated a new technology or AI capability and turned it into a practical, reliable product experience.
follow_ups: How did you handle non-determinism, latency, or failure modes so users could trust it?
How did you evaluate quality before and after shipping?
questions.carl_focus: Highlight evaluation rigor, UX guardrails, and what you learned about real-world reliability.
